organization: LO, the Danish Confederation of Trade Unions (Landsorganisationen i Danmark)
description: Her only job outside politics listed in her official CVs, before her election to the Folketing in November 2001.

Elected for Københavns Amtskreds (20 November 2001 – 13 November 2007), then Københavns Omegns Storkreds (13 November 2007 – 5 June 2019) and, since 5 June 2019, Nordjyllands Storkreds (North Jutland). Earlier in her parliamentary career she was the party's spokesperson on social affairs, culture and gender equality, according to the Folketing's biography.

role: Vice-chair of the Social Democratic parliamentary group (næstformand for folketingsgruppen)
organization: Socialdemokratiet, parliamentary group in the Folketing
description: Deputy leader of the Social Democrats' group in the Folketing while the party was in opposition.

organization: Government of Denmark (Thorning-Schmidt I and II cabinets)
description: Served in Helle Thorning-Schmidt's centre-left governments; according to Wikipedia her reforms covered early-retirement (førtidspension) and flex-job schemes and cash assistance (kontanthjælp), including lower benefits for young unemployed people.
Justice minister until the government left office after losing the June 2015 election.
Succeeded Helle Thorning-Schmidt, who resigned as party leader after the 18 June 2015 election. She has led the party into the 2019, 2022 and 2026 general elections, in all of which it came first.

Single-party Social Democratic minority government supported by the Social Liberals (RV), the Socialist People's Party (SF) and the Red–Green Alliance (EL) on the basis of a joint policy paper. It led the response to the COVID-19 pandemic and the 2020 mink cull, and after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine concluded the 6 March 2022 national compromise on security policy.

Coalition of the Social Democrats, Venstre and the Moderates (SVM) under the platform 'Ansvar for Danmark' of 14 December 2022, with Venstre leader Jakob Ellemann-Jensen (later Troels Lund Poulsen) as deputy prime minister and Moderates leader Lars Løkke Rasmussen as foreign minister. It held the rotating presidency of the Council of the EU in the second half of 2025. After the 24 March 2026 election Frederiksen tendered the government's resignation and stayed on as caretaker (fungerende) prime minister until 3 June 2026.

Four-party minority government of the Social Democrats, SF (Green Left), the Moderates and the Social Liberals (82 of 179 seats), formed after three rounds of negotiations, relying mainly on the Red–Green Alliance and the Alternative. Its platform, 'Det politiske grundlag for firkløverregeringen', was presented on 2 June 2026 and the ministers on 3 June 2026.
